meta.description: Machine-readable concept taxonomy aligned with the SimpleL7Proxy source code and documentation. Not intended for human consumption.

domains.name: Request Lifecycle
domains.description: End-to-end path a request travels from client to backend and back.

domains.name: Backend Management
domains.description: How the proxy discovers, probes, and selects backend hosts.

domains.name: Reliability
domains.description: Mechanisms that prevent failures from propagating to clients.

domains.name: Request Governance
domains.description: Validation and priority rules applied before a request enters the queue.

domains.name: Async Mode
domains.description: Long-running request handling that decouples client wait from backend processing.

domains.name: Observability
domains.description: How the proxy exposes telemetry about its own operation.

domains.name: Configuration Management
domains.description: How settings reach the proxy and when they take effect.

domains.name: Authentication and Security
domains.description: How the proxy authenticates to backends and restricts inbound callers.

domains.name: Deployment Architecture
domains.description: How the proxy is packaged and run on Azure.

domains.name: Protocol and Headers
domains.description: Named HTTP signals that cross the client-proxy and proxy-backend boundaries.

domains.name: Tokenomics
domains.description: Model routing, usage accounting, policy decisions, and associated telemetry.

concepts.name: Listener
concepts.definition: Accepts inbound HTTP requests and creates RequestData. /liveness, /readiness, and /startup are answered immediately; /health, /healthdetail, and /forcegc are queued as probe requests and bypass preprocessing, admission, and request validation. Ordinary requests pass through preprocessors, admission checks, authentication, profile enrichment, and header validation before queueing.

concepts.name: RequestData
concepts.definition: Per-request runtime state for the inbound request and its processing lifecycle: client context and streams, cached body bytes, headers, identity and priority, enqueue/expiry times, routing and attempt counters, event data, and optional async/background/recovery and Tokenomics state. Its computed RequestType distinguishes sync, async, background, background-check, and status-check flows.

concepts.name: Request Lifecycle Manager
concepts.definition: Checks TTL before backend work and coordinates status transitions across request types. When async mode is enabled, it updates Service Bus status and async RequestAPI status; successful Async and completed background-check requests become Completed only after blob writes finish. Background submissions and unfinished background checks retain their separate polling lifecycle.

concepts.name: Request Types
concepts.definition: Execution mode stored on RequestData to route responses and background work: Sync returns directly to the client; Async stores the response for later retrieval; AsyncBackground submits a backend batch operation; AsyncBackgroundCheck polls for its result; StatusCheck queries the request API without invoking the backend.

concepts.name: Enqueue
concepts.definition: Submitting a RequestData to the priority queue. For ordinary requests, the enqueue timestamp is set immediately before expiration is calculated and queue admission is attempted; relative TTL uses that timestamp.

concepts.name: Max Queue Length
concepts.definition: Queue admission threshold for ordinary incoming requests. Enqueue rejects with 429 when the observed queue count reaches MaxQueueLength; concurrent ordinary admissions can pass the check simultaneously. Requeues are allowed to exceed the threshold.

concepts.name: Priority Queue
concepts.definition: Sorted list using binary-search insertion. Lower primary priority sorts first; within a priority, higher secondary priority sorts first, then enqueue time. An any-priority worker takes the first item; a preferred-priority worker uses a binary-search lookup and can take another priority when its preference is unavailable. Priority-0 requests can be handed directly to a waiting worker or dispatched ahead of other queued requests.

concepts.name: Priority Level
concepts.definition: Integer assigned to every request. Lower numbers sort earlier in the queue, although preferred-priority workers can select another position.

concepts.name: Default Priority
concepts.definition: Priority level assigned when the request carries no matching PriorityKeyHeader value.

concepts.name: TTL (Time-to-Live)
concepts.definition: Expiration timestamp for a request, based on a relative or absolute TTL. It is checked before backend attempts; an expired request follows the 412 path. Async upgrade can recalculate expiration, and an async attempt's cancellation timer uses AsyncTimeout rather than the remaining TTL.

concepts.name: ProxyWorker
concepts.definition: Processes one dequeued request: applies Tokenomics policy and model transformation before backend selection, iterates eligible hosts with circuit checks, timeouts, retries and optional async coordination, then captures and streams the response to the client or blob storage. Usage extraction and metrics recording happen while the response is streamed. ProxyRequestHandler owns the worker loop and request-level state transitions.

concepts.name: Workers
concepts.definition: Count of ordinary proxy workers. WorkerFactory also creates a dedicated priority-0 probe worker. Cold setting; default is 10.

concepts.name: ProxyData
concepts.definition: Runtime object holding backend response status, response and content headers, the requested URL, backend host and latency, response time, and streaming/processor and usage metadata. The response body can be buffered bytes or an HttpResponseMessage retained for streaming; Dispose clears buffered bytes, disposes that response, and clears headers.

concepts.name: Pass-through
concepts.definition: Any backend status code in AcceptableStatusCodes is forwarded directly to the client without triggering retry or circuit recording.

concepts.name: Injected Response Headers
concepts.definition: Diagnostic headers the proxy can attach to forwarded backend responses. Header stripping and response paths affect which headers are actually returned.

concepts.name: Backend Host
concepts.definition: An upstream endpoint or logical backend configured with a numeric Host1..N key or a named Host_ or Host- key. Numeric discovery stops at the first missing host.

concepts.name: Connection String Format
concepts.definition: Per-host configuration using semicolon- or comma-delimited key=value entries. The parser rejects unknown keys; path, mode, processor, and per-host authentication options are specified in this format.

concepts.name: Legacy Format
concepts.definition: Legacy separate HostN, Probe_pathN, and IPN configuration. Global UseOAuth and OAuthAudience environment variables also supply legacy authentication defaults; per-host options use the connection-string format.

concepts.name: Path Prefix
concepts.definition: Path configured on a host for legacy host selection. Matching is case-insensitive; ordinary prefixes match at a path-segment boundary, while a trailing /* uses a string-prefix match. Query strings are excluded from matching. Named routes use their own prefix rules.

concepts.name: Catch-all Host
concepts.definition: A legacy host with an empty path, /, or /*. It is considered when no specific-path host matches, before filtering by request priority; named routes take precedence.

concepts.name: IP Override
concepts.definition: The ipaddress connection-string value is used in the APIM-mode probe URL. Forwarded requests build their destination URL from the configured host, not this field. Separately, APPENDHOSTSFILE can append legacy IP entries to /etc/hosts.

concepts.name: Strip Prefix
concepts.definition: When true (default), the matched path prefix is removed from the URL before forwarding. Set stripprefix=false to preserve the full original path.

concepts.name: Processor
concepts.definition: Named response stream processor configured on a host. ProxyWorker uses the configured processor for direct mode, supports AutoDetect, and can instead select response-header or model-mapping processing. OpenAI extracts token usage from supported responses.

concepts.name: Stream Processor Factory
concepts.definition: Creates processors by name with DefaultStream fallback for unknown names or construction failures. Response-header detection reads TOKENPROCESSOR only on HTTP 200; absent a recognized override, DefaultStream is used, including for event streams.

concepts.name: Response Format Mapping
concepts.definition: Maps generated text and available response metadata between OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages formats. JSON and SSE use separate parsers and writers; the mapper requires a supported source and target format and does not preserve every provider-specific field.

concepts.name: Direct Mode
concepts.definition: Backend mode where no health probe is sent and the host's probe success rate is treated as healthy. With no latency samples its average probe latency is 0 ms; circuit-breaker checks still apply to requests.

concepts.name: Indirect Mode
concepts.definition: Logical backend mode where the proxy never calls or probes the host. The host must name an APIM-mode gateway through via and belong to a named Path route. A gateway route selects that gateway when at least one configured logical host accepts the request priority.

concepts.name: Health Poller
concepts.definition: Background loop that probes probeable registered hosts at PollInterval ms intervals and tracks their rolling success rate and latency. Direct-mode, indirect-mode, and hosts with empty or / probe paths are not probed.

concepts.name: Probe Path
concepts.definition: URL path sent as a GET request to test backend health. Used by APIM mode and ignored by direct and indirect modes.

concepts.name: Success Rate
concepts.definition: Rolling percentage of successful probe responses for a probeable host after its first successful probe. Before that success, probe failures are ignored and the reported rate is 100%. The active-host health list uses the SuccessRate threshold.

concepts.name: Active Pool
concepts.definition: The health monitor's list of registered hosts whose success rate meets the configured threshold. It drives health reporting and readiness; the request iterator resolves candidates from the host snapshot rather than this active list.

concepts.name: Average Latency
concepts.definition: Probe latency averaged over up to 50 samples. Probeable hosts add a penalty based on failed-probe rate; non-probeable hosts use the raw average, normally 0 ms when no samples have been recorded.

concepts.name: BaseHostHealth
concepts.definition: Runtime object holding a host configuration, probe and request latency samples, and request error counts. Probeable and non-probeable subclasses calculate health differently; the associated HostConfig owns the circuit breaker.

concepts.name: Backend Selection Pipeline
concepts.definition: Selects the longest matching named path route when one matches and uses its host order; otherwise filters legacy hosts by path and request priority and orders them according to load-balance mode. Each candidate is subject to circuit-breaker checks.

concepts.name: IteratorFactory
concepts.definition: Creates a load-balance iterator for a given request path based on LoadBalanceMode configuration.

concepts.name: Path Filter
concepts.definition: When no named route matches, all matching legacy specific-path hosts are selected; only if none match are catch-all hosts selected. Priority filtering happens afterward, so an empty result after filtering does not fall back to catch-all. The first matched host determines the shared modified path.

concepts.name: Load Balance Mode
concepts.definition: Determines ordering of matched legacy hosts. Named routes instead preserve their configured host order.

concepts.name: Host Priority Filter
concepts.definition: The acceptablepriorities host key restricts a host to positive request priority values separated by colons. An omitted value or * accepts any priority. Named routes apply this filter to their configured hosts; legacy matching applies it after choosing specific or catch-all hosts.

concepts.name: Round-Robin Iterator
concepts.definition: Uses an atomic counter to select successive positions among candidate hosts. Concurrent requests and circuit-breaker checks can affect which hosts are actually attempted.

concepts.name: Latency Iterator
concepts.definition: Orders candidate hosts by ascending AverageLatency, including the probe failure-rate penalty for probeable hosts.

concepts.name: Time-to-First-Byte Iterator
concepts.definition: Orders hosts by ascending observed backend response-header latency.

concepts.name: Priority Group Iterator
concepts.definition: Orders candidate hosts by ascending configured priority group, with randomized ordering among hosts in the same group.

concepts.name: Random Iterator
concepts.definition: Shuffles candidate hosts randomly when creating a per-request iterator and when resetting its traversal.

concepts.name: Shared Iterator
concepts.definition: Iterator shared across concurrent requests to the same normalized path when enabled for round-robin or random ordering. Named routes and configurations with non-default priority groups or priority restrictions use per-request iterators. Shared iteration uses a circular cursor; stale iterators are periodically removed.

concepts.name: Iteration Mode
concepts.definition: Controls retry breadth. SinglePass limits a traversal to one lap; shared iterators cap actual attempts by host count. Concurrent round-robin requests can advance the shared counter between selections, so a lap does not guarantee distinct hosts. MultiPass repeats traversal until MaxAttempts is reached; set MaxAttempts to 0 to disable that cap.

concepts.name: Max Attempts
concepts.definition: Maximum total host attempts in MultiPass mode, including prior attempts across requeue cycles. Set to 0 to disable the attempt-count limit. Hosts skipped because their circuit is OPEN do not consume an attempt.

concepts.name: Circuit Breaker
concepts.definition: Per-host failure counter with a sliding time window. The failure-count blocked state starts when the count reaches CBErrorThreshold; a separate retry deadline controls request admission and can also be set by Retry-After before the threshold is reached.

concepts.name: CLOSED State
concepts.definition: Normal circuit breaker state. Requests are forwarded to the host.

concepts.name: OPEN State
concepts.definition: A host is skipped while its circuit-breaker retry deadline is in the future. Skips do not consume the MaxAttempts budget; a Retry-After-derived deadline can extend beyond the failure-window deadline.

concepts.name: Sliding Window
concepts.definition: Only failures timestamped within the last CBTimeslice seconds count toward the threshold. Older entries are pruned automatically.

concepts.name: Auto-Recovery
concepts.definition: The failure-count blocked state clears when enough failures expire to bring the count below the threshold. Request admission uses a separate retry deadline, which can remain in the future due to Retry-After.

concepts.name: Progressive Delay
concepts.definition: The circuit breaker reports backpressure delays as its failure count approaches CBErrorThreshold. Threshold bucket counts use integer truncation, so small thresholds can cross buckets earlier than their nominal percentages. At or above the threshold, the reported delay is 1000 ms.

concepts.name: Global Blocked Check
concepts.definition: Static circuit-breaker registry check that reports whether all registered child circuit breakers are blocked by failure count; it returns false when none are registered. Counts are refreshed by a 500 ms timer. The parent breaker's GetMsToNextRetry uses this check; request iteration separately checks candidate retry deadlines.

concepts.name: Acceptable Status Codes
concepts.definition: Backend status codes accepted without retry based on the status alone. The circuit breaker ignores an acceptable code only when the attempt is not also marked as a failure.

concepts.name: Retry
concepts.definition: Advancing to another iterator candidate after retryable backend responses or attempt errors. Non-acceptable status codes do not all follow the same retry path; circuit-open candidates are skipped without a backend attempt.

concepts.name: Requeue
concepts.definition: Returning a request to the priority queue for a later processing cycle. Backend 429 responses with S7PREQUEUE:true contribute retry delays; after attempts are exhausted the shortest delay is used unless the MultiPass attempt cap has been reached. S7PRequeueException carries a millisecond delay; the worker can defer handling it while trying other hosts, then the request handler schedules the delayed requeue. The delay worker resets per-cycle backend attempts and incomplete-attempt details but retains lifetime attempts. Shutdown cancellation applies to async delays, which abort and persist async requests for reprocessing; non-async delays are not cancellable. All-blocked circuits and Tokenomics policy can also cause requeue.

concepts.name: S7PREQUEUE
concepts.definition: Response header a backend sets on a 429 reply to make the request eligible for delayed requeue after the proxy finishes trying available hosts.

concepts.name: Retry-After
concepts.definition: For backend 429 requeue, the proxy parses retry-after-ms as integer milliseconds, otherwise Retry-After as integer seconds, defaulting to 1000 ms. It uses the shortest eligible delay seen after host attempts are exhausted. Circuit-breaker Retry-After handling is separate.

concepts.name: Timeout
concepts.definition: For synchronous requests, the per-host-attempt cancellation window in milliseconds is the lesser of remaining TTL and the configured or request-overridden timeout. Async-enabled requests instead use AsyncTimeout for the attempt cancellation timer; TTL is checked separately before an attempt.

concepts.name: AsyncTriggerTimeout
concepts.definition: For eligible async requests, the delay measured from enqueue before the async worker attempts to release the client with a 202 response and continue processing in the background.

concepts.name: AsyncTimeout
concepts.definition: Per-attempt backend cancellation timeout in milliseconds for requests enabled for async processing, including before the 202 response is sent.

concepts.name: AsyncTTLSecs
concepts.definition: Default TTL in seconds used when the async worker recalculates request expiration. A supplied TTL header still takes precedence, and a relative TTL is measured from the request's enqueue time.

concepts.name: Validation Pipeline
concepts.definition: Ordered validation checks for non-probe requests that pass preprocessing and admission checks. Probe requests bypass these checks; plugins and admission limits can reject a request before validation.

steps.when: ValidateAuthConfig enables key, oauth2, or mixed mode

concepts.name: App ID Validation
concepts.definition: Step 2 of the validation pipeline when enabled. Checks the caller's Entra Application ID against a remote allowlist before header stripping and profile/header validation checks. Designed for deployments with more than 13 App IDs (Entra's built-in limit).

concepts.name: Inbound Key Validation
concepts.definition: Step 1 optional auth gate. In key or mixed mode, the proxy checks the configured inbound header against ValidateAuthKey1 or ValidateAuthKey2; bearer values in oauth2 or mixed mode use token validation.

concepts.name: Inbound OAuth Validation
concepts.definition: Validates inbound bearer tokens in oauth2 or mixed mode using mandatory issuer, audience, lifetime, and RS256 signature validation. Signing keys are loaded and rotated through the issuer's HTTPS OIDC metadata endpoint.

concepts.name: Request Preprocessor Plugins
concepts.definition: Configured IRequestPreprocessorPlugin implementations are invoked in registration order for non-probe requests before admission checks, validation, and enqueue. A plugin can mutate the request or stop processing with a status and message. The allow-all implementation is used when no valid plugin is configured.

concepts.name: Header Stripping
concepts.definition: Step 3 of the validation pipeline. Removes headers listed in DisallowedHeaders silently. No error is returned to the caller.

concepts.name: Required Headers
concepts.definition: List of header names that must be non-empty on non-probe requests reaching validation. The first missing header returns 417.

concepts.name: Disallowed Headers
concepts.definition: Headers stripped silently from the incoming request before profile enrichment. A ValidateHeaders rule with an allowlist header automatically adds that header to this list; an inline-only rule does not.

concepts.name: Header Validation Rule
concepts.definition: ValidateHeaders rules compare a source header against inline allowed values and an optional comma-separated allowlist header injected from the user profile. Matching is case-insensitive; prefix-wildcard rules interpret a trailing * as a prefix match. Legacy SourceHeader=AllowlistHeader mappings remain supported.
side_effects: when mapped, auto-adds AllowlistHeader to RequiredHeaders and DisallowedHeaders

concepts.name: App ID Allowlist
concepts.definition: File, HTTP(S), or azblob source returning permitted Entra Application IDs. Enforced at step 2 of the validation pipeline; removed IDs are soft-deleted for the configured grace period before expiring.

concepts.name: User Profile
concepts.definition: Per-user JSON records loaded from a file, HTTP(S), or azblob source. Profile fields can supply request headers, async configuration, and shared or inline rules. Removed profiles are soft-deleted for the configured grace period; requests can still use their snapshot during that period, but async opt-in rejects soft-deleted profiles. Profile headers exclude internal-* and deletion-marker fields.

profile_fields.description: Unique identifier matched against the incoming request header.
Priority tier value mapped via PriorityKeys.
Enables async mode and sets per-user blob container and Service Bus topic.
Assigns named shared profile rules; when present, this takes precedence over inline rules.
Any other key is injected as an HTTP request header.

concepts.name: User ID
concepts.definition: The field named by UserIDFieldName identifies each profile record. The incoming UserProfileHeader supplies the profile lookup value; UniqueUserHeaders are concatenated in order to construct the request's queue-accounting user ID, which defaults to defaultUser when all values are empty.

concepts.name: S7PPriorityKey Profile Field
concepts.definition: A profile field injected into request headers. When the configured PriorityKeyHeader names that field, its value is matched against PriorityKeys to assign a priority tier.

concepts.name: async-config Profile Field
concepts.definition: User profile field enabling async mode for a specific user. Requires enabled=true and valid containername and topic values. Optional timeout is a positive number of seconds defaulting to 3600; generatesas defaults to false and is retained but the current response path does not generate SAS tokens.
concepts.behavior_note: generatesas is parsed and retained, but the current blob URI path returns base URIs and does not generate SAS tokens.

concepts.name: Profile Refresh
concepts.definition: UserProfile reloads configured sources at UserConfigRefreshIntervalSecs (default 1 hour) and publishes parsed profile snapshots. Failed reads retry after 3 seconds and retain prior data; removed profiles and auth app IDs are soft-deleted for UserSoftDeleteTTLMinutes. With configured sources and UserConfigRequired=true, missing initial data or data stale beyond that grace period prevents profile readiness. If all sources are unset, the service registers ready even when UserConfigRequired=true; request-time profile checks can still reject missing profiles.

concepts.name: Suspended User
concepts.definition: When profiles are enabled and the profile lookup header is present, a user whose ID appears in the suspended users list receives 403 before profile data is applied.

concepts.name: Priority Mapping
concepts.definition: Maps a request header value to an internal priority integer. Worker allocations specify preferred priorities for queue dispatch.
concepts.constraint: If PriorityKeys and PriorityValues have different counts, the parser replaces PriorityValues with the default priority repeated for each key. If allocated worker counts exceed Workers, the parser raises Workers to the allocation total.

concepts.name: Priority Key Header
concepts.definition: Name of the request header the proxy inspects to determine priority tier. Default: S7PPriorityKey.

concepts.name: Priority Keys
concepts.definition: Comma-separated list of expected header values. Each entry maps 1:1 to the corresponding entry in PriorityValues.

concepts.name: Priority Values
concepts.definition: Comma-separated list of internal priority integers, in 1:1 correspondence with PriorityKeys.

concepts.name: Priority Workers
concepts.definition: PriorityLevel:WorkerCount pairs used to assign preferred priorities when workers start. Workers can process other priorities if their preferred priority is unavailable. The startup parser reads PriorityWorkers into PriorityWorkerDict; WorkerFactory copies that dictionary once when creating workers. Changing the warm PriorityWorker property does not recreate or reassign existing workers.

concepts.name: Per-user Throttling
concepts.definition: A secondary queue priority favors requests from users whose tracked share of active requests is below UserPriorityThreshold. It does not change the primary priority tier or reject requests. UserPriority copies the threshold at singleton construction and does not observe warm config refreshes, so the active threshold requires restart to change.

concepts.name: Async Mode
concepts.definition: Asynchronous handling for eligible incoming requests. It requires AsyncModeEnabled, an available non-null blob writer, valid enabled async settings in the selected user profile, and a per-request opt-in header parsed as true. Upgrade is still conditional on response timing and blob queue pressure.
enablement_levels: AsyncModeEnabled=true and an available non-null blob writer
enabled async-config with valid container and topic in the selected user profile

concepts.name: Opt-in Header
concepts.definition: Per-request header clients set to a Boolean true value to request async processing. This opt-in alone does not guarantee an async upgrade. Default header name: S7PAsyncMode.

concepts.name: Async Upgrade
concepts.definition: An eligible request can be released with a 202 and blob URIs after the async trigger delay. If the backend response arrives before startup, the async worker is canceled and processing continues synchronously; initialization failure or blob queue pressure can also prevent upgrade.

concepts.name: 202 Accepted Response
concepts.definition: HTTP 202 returned after async upgrade. The JSON body and x-Data-Blob-URI and x-Header-Blob-URI response headers identify the result blobs.

concepts.name: Result Blob
concepts.definition: Azure Blob Storage object used for an async response. Data is streamed to a lazily created blob and headers are stored separately. Base URIs are returned in the 202 response body and headers before the blobs necessarily exist.

concepts.name: Blob Lifecycle Policy
concepts.definition: External Azure Storage lifecycle management rule used to delete result blobs. The proxy does not configure or enforce blob deletion.

concepts.name: Service Bus Status
concepts.definition: Async status uses two distinct Service Bus paths: SBTopicService publishes ServiceBusStatusMessage notifications to the request's configured topic (default status), while SBQueueService batches RequestAPIDocument status updates to AsyncSBQueue (default requeststatus). AsyncFeeder separately consumes the feeder queue and restores or creates requests. Enqueue and delivery are not guaranteed.

concepts.name: Status Events
concepts.definition: Values in the Service Bus status enum. Updates are attempted for requests while runAsync is true; enum membership does not guarantee every value is emitted for every request.

concepts.name: Async Blob Worker
concepts.definition: BlobWorkerPump routes each blob to a worker channel by container/blob hash and batches small-blob uploads for the same container. Within each batch, duplicate writes to a blob are deduplicated to the last write. The DI defaults are a 10,000-operation total queue, 100 ms batch wait, and 25-item batch; total capacity is divided across workers, and a per-worker capacity of zero creates an unbounded channel. Response bodies use a separate direct streaming store and bypass this queue. AsyncBlobMaxQueue is an upgrade/readiness threshold, not the pump's configured queue capacity.

concepts.name: Async Worker
concepts.definition: Coordinates async upgrade and recovery. AsyncFeeder waits for startup readiness, consumes the feeder queue one message at a time, and enqueues requests with a recovery processor; AsyncRequestHydrator restores request state and response streams, while OpenAIBackgroundRequest prepares background-status checks. Before the first backend send, the request can be persisted. AsyncWorker waits for AsyncTriggerTimeout when the configured delay exceeds 10 ms before attempting the 202 upgrade, and proceeds only when blob queue depth is below AsyncBlobMaxQueue. After upgrade, clients receive blob URIs; response bodies stream directly to blob storage, headers use the file-store write path, and completion status is set only after blob writes are flushed/disposed. Background checks buffer responses before deciding whether to publish a completed result.

concepts.name: Request API
concepts.definition: Azure Functions subsystem that consumes ServiceBusQueue messages into Cosmos DB request documents, preserving existing fields omitted from updates. Anonymous GET checkStatus/{guid} returns 400 for an invalid GUID, 404 for a missing document, or 200 with Guid, Status, and the incremented CheckCount, writing the updated document back to Cosmos DB. Every minute, ReFeeder changes NeedsReprocessing documents to ReSubmitted and publishes them to SBFeederQueue; backgroundReqChecker publishes BackgroundProcessing background documents for checking while persisting a ReSubmitted copy.

concepts.name: Streaming Microservice
concepts.definition: Function-authorized GET/POST Azure Function that fetches the absolute URL supplied by the url query parameter and streams its response through a selected processor. A valid differing sourceModel/targetModel pair in model.APIFormat form selects model mapping before an explicit processor; otherwise processor selection uses the explicit name or upstream headers/content type. Invalid model pairs fall back to normal processing. Mapping preserves JSON versus SSE framing based on upstream text/event-stream. Processor statistics are emitted to Application Insights. Upstream-response caching is compile-time opt-in and disabled in the checked-in source.

concepts.name: ProxyEvent
concepts.definition: Event object containing a key/value dictionary plus fields such as type, status, method, URI, duration, and message ID. SendEvent routes by type to enabled destinations. Its serialized sink envelope adds Type, MID, Status, Method, and common fields as strings; ConvertToJson alone serializes only dictionary entries and supplied extra properties.

concepts.name: Event Headers
concepts.definition: Common event fields supplied by ICommonEventData. The built-in implementation supplies Ver, Replica, and ContainerApp; the SendEvent sink envelope also supplies status and method.

concepts.name: Event Destination Filtering
concepts.definition: LogToConsole, LogToEvents, and LogToAI independently select event categories. * includes all categories and a -category entry excludes that category. These selections refresh when their warm settings change; console output helpers have separate behavior from SendEvent.

concepts.name: CompositeEventClient
concepts.definition: Fan-out dispatcher that sends each submitted serialized event to registered event logger backends. ProxyEvent filters event types before sending to this dispatcher. Uses a FrozenDictionary snapshot for lock-free dispatch.

concepts.name: Event Logger Backend
concepts.definition: Named sink that receives serialized JSON ProxyEvents. Built-in values are file and eventhub; none disables event sinks. Custom backends implement IEventClient and optionally IHostedService.

concepts.name: Custom Event Logger
concepts.definition: User-supplied IEventClient selected by fully qualified type name. IHostedService implementations are also started by the host and can self-register with CompositeEventClient.

concepts.name: Application Insights
concepts.definition: Primary production telemetry sink. Receives structured telemetry (requests, dependencies, exceptions) via TelemetryClient.

concepts.name: Event Hubs
concepts.definition: Streaming telemetry sink for serialized JSON events. It requires an Event Hub name and either a connection string or namespace; a configured connection string takes precedence. The client batches events and attempts reconnects on transport recovery.

concepts.name: Log File
concepts.definition: Local JSON-lines file sink. Buffers events and flushes at 10 events or every 2 seconds; it attempts hourly rotation by renaming the file with a UTC hour suffix.

concepts.name: Batch Message Pump
concepts.definition: In-memory batching mechanism used by event sinks and Service Bus senders. Failed sends are requeued for retry; an item that cannot fit in an empty transport batch is dropped. Shutdown waits for the queue up to a configured interval before initiating final drain, but that interval is not a deadline on the final drain or transport calls.

concepts.name: Token Telemetry
concepts.definition: Usage counts extracted by supported response processors and logged per request. The Tokenomics processor handles JSON and SSE usage and can capture cached input and safety signals; usage may be unavailable.

concepts.name: /liveness Endpoint
concepts.definition: The proxy's own endpoint returns 200 OK while running. Sidecar behavior differs: .NET GET returns 503 after a previously received status update becomes more than 20 seconds old, but .NET HEAD remains 200; Python liveness GET and HEAD remain 200 independently of status updates.

responses.200: process running, except for stale-update .NET sidecar GET
responses.503: .NET sidecar GET with a previously received status update older than 20 seconds

concepts.name: /readiness Endpoint
concepts.definition: Returns 200 when startup readiness is satisfied, at least one host is active, backend backpressure is absent, the event client is healthy, event backlog is within limits, and blob queue depth is within the configured threshold; otherwise returns 503.

responses.503: startup, host, event backlog, or blob queue health criteria failed

concepts.name: /startup Endpoint
concepts.definition: Returns 200 when startup readiness is complete, at least one host is active, backend backpressure is absent, the event client is healthy and within its backlog limit, and blob queue depth is within its configured threshold; otherwise returns 503.

concepts.name: Sidecar Mode
concepts.definition: Isolation pattern where a separate HealthProbe container handles orchestration probes and the proxy pushes startup and readiness state every 5 seconds. After a received update, .NET GET liveness, readiness, and startup fail with 503 when the update is more than 20 seconds old; its HEAD handlers do not check staleness. Python readiness and startup GET/HEAD fail at 10 seconds, while its liveness remains independent. Before any update, readiness and startup begin in their zero-host failure states.

concepts.name: Health Probe Implementations
concepts.definition: .NET and Python sidecar servers expose GET/HEAD liveness, readiness, and startup probes on HEALTHPROBE_PORT (default 9000), plus GET /internal/update-status requiring readiness and startup query parameters. Missing or unparseable status values return 400. Their stale-update and HEAD semantics differ; they are not behaviorally identical implementations. StartupWorkersNotReady is not explicitly rejected by either sidecar startup handler.

concepts.name: Warm Setting
concepts.definition: Configuration category eligible for refresh from Azure App Configuration when the Sentinel value changes. The default polling interval is 30 seconds; actual timing depends on the configured interval and successful refresh. Individual consumers may apply values only at startup.

concepts.name: Cold Setting
concepts.definition: Configuration value published to Azure App Configuration but taking effect only after a container restart.

concepts.name: Hidden Setting
concepts.definition: Configuration category not published to Azure App Configuration. Hidden values include settings supplied directly through other configuration sources as well as values parsed from composite settings.

concepts.name: Sentinel
concepts.definition: Special key (Warm:Sentinel) in Azure App Configuration. Each proxy instance polls the selected label and, when the value changes, downloads configuration and applies recognized nonempty Warm values. Refresh timing and consumer behavior can differ across instances.

concepts.name: Composite Connection String
concepts.definition: Semicolon or comma-delimited key=value string encoding multiple related settings in one environment variable.

concepts.name: App Configuration Label
concepts.definition: Label filter applied when reading from Azure App Configuration. Allows isolated setting namespaces per environment.

concepts.name: Refresh Interval
concepts.definition: How often in seconds the proxy polls the Sentinel key in Azure App Configuration.

concepts.name: Profile Configuration Publishing
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp stages a shared profile document separately from labeled App Configuration values. Import accepts legacy inline rules; export validates identities, fields and rule assignments and emits profiles followed by one S7PRules library entry. Save config.json stages validated JSON and the profile source URL; the page-level Save changes publishes the profile blob before submitting the App Configuration update. These are separate write operations.

concepts.name: Stream Flush Interval
concepts.definition: Cold setting in milliseconds that controls how often StreamFlusher runs and flushes tracked active response streams.

concepts.name: Configuration Plugin
concepts.definition: Startup extension selected by EnvPluginClass that supplies environment-specific identity values before the proxy services are registered. The built-in Azure plugin maps CONTAINER_APP_NAME to ContainerApp, CONTAINER_APP_REVISION to ReplicaName, and CONTAINER_APP_REPLICA_NAME to Revision.

concepts.name: Backend Token Provider
concepts.definition: Outbound OAuth token implementation registered at startup through AuthProviders and selected per backend by the authprovider connection-string key using its simple class name, matched case-insensitively. The default AzureProvider obtains and caches tokens by audience using DefaultAzureCredential, refreshes before expiry, and waits in 100 ms intervals when a requested token is not yet available.

concepts.name: Async Request Backup
concepts.definition: Async request metadata is serialized as version-1 JSON in a blob named by request GUID, with request body bytes stored separately as a .body blob. Restore accepts version 1 or missing version (treated as version 1), repopulates request state, resets per-attempt counters, and uses an empty body if no body blob exists. The null serializer used when async storage is disabled performs no backup or restore.

concepts.name: Managed Identity
concepts.definition: Azure-managed identity can supply credentials for backends, App Configuration, Event Hubs, Blob Storage, and Service Bus. The default provider uses DefaultAzureCredential, whose credential chain can also select other credential sources.

concepts.name: OAuth2 Bearer Token
concepts.definition: For OAuth2 host authentication, the proxy obtains a token for the configured audience from the selected backend token provider and sends it as Authorization: Bearer. The default provider uses Azure credentials; a custom provider can implement different token acquisition.

concepts.name: Startup Readiness Gate
concepts.definition: Startup waits for all participants required by configuration to register ready: backends, backend tokens, workers, user profiles, event client, and Tokenomics when enabled, plus async templates, blob writer, and Service Bus participants when async mode is enabled. Program logs startup completion after this gate; the probe listener remains active through service draining and stops last. MarkNotReady updates diagnostic state but does not reset the one-shot startup completion task.

concepts.name: Backend API Key
concepts.definition: The api-key or api_key host option selects API-key authentication. The proxy replaces the configured outbound header with the key; api-key-header controls the header name and defaults to api-key. Authentication mode is selected while parsing entries, so avoid mixing API-key and OAuth options.

concepts.name: Keyless Auth
concepts.definition: Configuration pattern using usemi=true and audience=https://cognitiveservices.azure.com to eliminate API key management for Azure OpenAI and AI Foundry backends.

concepts.name: VNet Deployment
concepts.definition: Deployment pattern that integrates the Container Apps environment with a Virtual Network. In the Bicep deployment, PRIVATE_NETWORK_DEPLOYMENT controls whether a newly created environment is internal; network integration alone does not guarantee that all dependencies are private.

concepts.name: Azure Container Apps
concepts.definition: Primary hosting platform for SimpleL7Proxy. Provides ingress, auto-scaling, managed identity, and revision management.

concepts.name: Container Image
concepts.definition: Docker image pushed to Azure Container Registry (ACR) and deployed to Azure Container Apps.

concepts.name: Sidecar Deployment
concepts.definition: Two-container ACA revision: proxy container on port 8000 and health probe container on port 9000. Both containers share localhost networking within the revision.

concepts.name: Parameters File
concepts.definition: Local parameter file consumed by the VNet provisioning script for Azure target, network, and subnet values.

concepts.name: CompanionApp Deployment Setup
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp offers simple and advanced deployment setup, validates deployment parameters, and generates Bicep bundles, staged Portal/ARM templates, or Standalone deployment artifacts.

concepts.name: APIM Integration
concepts.definition: Integration pattern using Azure API Management as a gateway for SimpleL7Proxy. Capabilities such as caching, content inspection, rate limits, quotas, and mutual TLS depend on the APIM configuration; integration alone does not enable them.

concepts.name: AI Foundry Integration
concepts.definition: Direct or APIM-mediated connection to Azure OpenAI and AI Foundry model endpoints. A supported usage processor can extract token counts from responses.

concepts.name: Named Path Route
concepts.definition: A Path_* or Path-* setting associates a segment-boundary URL prefix with an ordered list of host keys and can override iteration mode and maximum attempts. A route uses either direct hosts or logical hosts sharing one APIM gateway; it cannot mix those forms. The longest matching prefix wins; a valid S7P-Iterator request header takes precedence over the route iteration mode. A matched route with no eligible hosts does not fall back to a broader route.

concepts.name: Tokenomics
concepts.definition: Request policy and accounting functionality using configured options and metrics to evaluate requests, route models, and record decisions and outcomes. Tokenomics is disabled at runtime when the metrics-server endpoint is missing or invalid, or options cannot be parsed.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Policy
concepts.definition: Evaluates the first matching request condition and configured action. Abuse precedes administrator override; then hourly, daily, and monthly quotas, budget conditions, capacity, queue depth, and the default action are checked. Limits and exceed actions are selected from privileged workload, premium workload, model-specific, then default settings. The current condition builder populates token quotas but not budget-exceeded fields.

concepts.name: Model and API Routing
concepts.definition: ModelHostOptions associates models with enabled hosts and API path options. An absent model entry leaves the original path unrestricted; a configured model requires an enabled matching host and API. API options select the original path, the catalog default path, or an overridden path. When Tokenomics is enabled, the chosen path replaces the iterator's modified path.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Usage
concepts.definition: The Tokenomics response processor extracts usage and safety signals from JSON or SSE while forwarding response bytes. Usage normalization tries the request model's preferred provider schema, then other supported schemas. Usage availability must be checked separately from token counts; cached input tokens are a subset of input tokens.

concepts.name: Model Token Pricing
concepts.definition: ModelCostPerToken stores USD prices per token for non-cached input, cached input, and output. Calculated cost applies the input rate to input tokens excluding cached tokens, then adds cached-input and output costs. The CompanionApp pricing editor displays rates per million tokens by default and converts entered values to per-token prices before staging them.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Metrics Server
concepts.definition: The proxy sends deltas to MetricsServer, which keeps in-memory UTC hour, day, and month totals by case-insensitive user/model and by model across users. Records whose Day is not the current UTC date are ignored; accepted deltas enter the server's current ingestion hour rather than an hour derived from TimestampUtc. GET /tokenomics/metrics/lookup requires u and m, returning 400 when either is blank. Calculated budgets use the currently loaded model prices, with unpriced models returning zero budget values. The proxy uses a 400 ms lookup timeout, caches responses with a five-second expiry checked by a five-second cleanup loop, and returns a default metric on lookup failure. All server totals are lost on restart.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Metric Batch Delivery
concepts.definition: The proxy retains metric batches in memory and polls the MetricsServer every five seconds while batches remain. It resends batches not reported as pending or processed and removes them when the server reports them processed; local retention is not durable across process restarts.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Batch Admission and Acknowledgement
concepts.definition: POST /tokenomics/metrics/upload queues manifest batch IDs and raw CSV sections, returning 202 with PendingBatches and ProcessedBatches rather than waiting for aggregation. Replica identity comes from query parameter r, defaulting to unknown. Admission deduplicates case-insensitive replica/batch pairs while active and within a 65536-entry processed history per replica; responses expose at most 10 recent processed IDs. The queue drains every second. Malformed rows are skipped, and invalid-header or missing sections can still be marked processed, so acknowledgement is not proof every row was recorded. Exceptions retry a section without rolling back rows already applied. State and deduplication history are process-local and lost on restart.

concepts.name: Metrics Server Configuration
concepts.definition: MetricsServer reads listener and generic-series settings from environment variables at startup, defaulting invalid or out-of-range integers. Its default port is 9100, request-body limit is 4194304 bytes, and generic-series ring defaults are 60 buckets of 60 seconds with a 100000-series admission threshold; these ring settings do not bound the separate Tokenomics totals store. An optional AppConfigurationEndpoint enables a startup download and 15-minute polling of an exact AppConfigurationLabel, with an empty label selecting unlabeled settings. Successful downloads replace the cached configuration snapshot; Warm:Tokenomics:Options supplies current pricing, retaining the last parsed settings on failure. GET/HEAD /health, /liveness, and /readiness return 200 independently of configuration-download success.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Summary Events
concepts.definition: Tokenomics emits PolicyDecision and RequestOutcome records. A policy evaluation and a backend outcome are different records. On backend outcomes, UsageAvailable is based on whether a usage object was supplied, not on that object's UsageAvailable value; exception outcomes set it to false.

concepts.name: Profile Rules
concepts.definition: A profile can assign named shared rules or contain inline rules. If S7PRules is present, shared assignments take precedence over inline rules. ProfileEnricher evaluates top-level rules against the same pre-rule request context and applies their resulting headers in order, so later results can overwrite earlier headers but do not feed later rule conditions. Missing fields satisfy notEquals and notContains conditions.

concepts.name: Coordinated Shutdown
concepts.definition: Stops accepting requests, stops async/requeue producers, expels async work, and signals workers to drain. TerminationGracePeriodSeconds controls how long shutdown waits before logging a grace-period warning; the service then still waits for the queue to drain before stopping backends, IShutdownParticipant services in ascending ShutdownOrder, token providers, Service Bus, blob workers, probes, and event clients.

concepts.name: Host Configuration Snapshot
concepts.definition: Backend hosts and named routes are built and validated as a candidate snapshot before activation. Invalid route or host references reject the candidate; the active snapshot remains available. In-flight requests can retain references to an older snapshot.

concepts.name: Model Hierarchy
concepts.definition: Configured ordered model/API destinations support adjacent model upgrades and downgrades. The longest matching model prefix selects a hierarchy; at the destination, the current API is preferred, followed by an unspecified API, then the first configured API.

concepts.name: Model Parameter Mapping
concepts.definition: When rewriting a request for a different model, model-family mappings determine which top-level parameters are removed or renamed. These scalar parameter mappings are separate from API response-format conversion; unknown or decision model families use empty maps.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Options
concepts.definition: TokenomicsOptions is a composite string of key=value settings. Invalid or unknown entries are skipped and reported as ignored fields while valid entries are applied; a malformed overall value can fail parsing. Defaults are provided by TokenomicsSettings. When loading App Configuration, CompanionApp stages canonicalized options for its configured default label if parsing succeeds with ignored fields; saving is required to persist that cleanup.

concepts.name: LLM API Catalog
concepts.definition: Catalog metadata defines API identities, display names, default paths, and aliases. Request-path parsing matches exact paths and longest suffixes, ignores query strings, and resolves paths shared by chat and vision APIs to the non-vision identity.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Dashboard
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp buffers validated live Tokenomics summaries, retaining the latest 10000 received records. A one-second timer checks for publication: live snapshots refresh after new records, a pricing-context change, or a 60-tick window refresh. Hourly, daily and monthly selections use UTC calendar boundaries, not rolling durations. Base overview usage aggregation selects the last received RequestOutcome per MID. Spend estimates use currently loaded model prices rather than historical billing rates. The store initially publishes simulated sample data until a non-sample publication replaces it.

concepts.name: CompanionApp App Configuration Publishing
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp maintains loaded values and editable drafts for published Warm and Cold settings across labels. Creating a label can use proxy defaults or copy saved source values without writing immediately. Publication writes changed settings for the target label, writes Warm:Sentinel afterward, and re-downloads settings to verify submitted values, deletions, and the sentinel. Individual writes are sequential rather than atomic.

concepts.name: CompanionApp Identity List Publishing
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp Applications and Suspended Users editors read and directly upload JSON arrays to azblob sources using their own Save buttons. When a source URL is missing, the editor can stage one using the configured profile storage account and container, defaulting the container to profiles and using appids.json or suspended.json. Uploading list data and publishing its staged App Configuration URL are separate operations.

concepts.name: CompanionApp User Preferences
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp serializes request selections, user-identity and custom-header overrides, supported display and storage overrides, and onboarding progress as base64-encoded camelCase JSON in the chat_tester_prefs browser cookie through JavaScript interop. Saving builds a snapshot against configured defaults, loading applies available overrides to live settings, and reset restores defaults and clears the cookie. Dedicated authorization settings are excluded; custom header names and values are serialized. Empty custom-header arrays and blank identity strings are not restored, and ResponseFormat is not persisted by this service.

concepts.name: CompanionApp Observability Publications
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp centrally publishes immutable monitor and metric-catalog snapshots on the configured monitor refresh cadence, defaulting to five seconds. Publications continue during idle periods. Analytics projections are cached per publication and filter query; request-inspector rows and nested lifecycle data are detached for each circuit rather than exposing ingestion-owned mutable objects.

concepts.name: Observed Usage Projection
concepts.definition: CompanionApp Insights normalizes nonnegative integer Usage.* header values and numeric usage fields from ordinary JSON response bodies, including response.usage. Duplicate normalized metrics retain their maximum value rather than being summed. A missing total_tokens is derived only when both input/prompt and output/completion counts exist. This consumer-side projection is separate from the proxy's Tokenomics usage decoder; its body parser does not decode SSE.

concepts.name: Observed Backend Attribution
concepts.definition: CompanionApp endpoint analytics reconstruct model-to-backend activity from backendLog target entries and fall back to captured x-backend-label fields. Exact backend-log strings are deduplicated across backend events and proxy summaries. The last target in a log receives the source event's HTTP failure classification; earlier targets receive inferred failures only when target-specific throttling text is present. These reconstructed attempt counts and classifications are not independently captured outcomes for every target.

concepts.name: Tokenomics Local Event Replay
concepts.definition: Local replay validates the complete NDJSON input before startup, requiring object records with scalar fields and a Type. Tokenomics summaries additionally require valid record-kind-specific fields. Replay consumes ten file records per second, aggregates matching Tokenomics summaries, anchors period windows to the latest received summary timestamp when available, and retains its final snapshot at EOF. File replay disables the live Event Hub reader. When no configured prices are available, replay supplies sample model prices.

concepts.name: Recorded Policy Decision Analysis
concepts.definition: Policy analysis counts requests using their latest recorded policy evaluation within the selected snapshot, ordered by timestamp and evaluation sequence. Action totals and recent rows retain individual deduplicated evaluations; None and Bypass are excluded from action totals. AllowedWithChanges is displayed as Modified without collapsing Requeued, Throttled or Pending into Allowed. Policy outcomes are not final HTTP outcomes. Uncaptured configured actions, thresholds, token usage, governance flags and policy versions remain explicitly unavailable. CSV export includes every evaluation matching the recent-table outcome filter, not only its visible page.

concepts.name: Recorded Model Routing Analysis
concepts.definition: Routing analysis correlates policy and outcome records by MID within the selected snapshot and counts each request once. It compares the earliest recorded requested model with the latest outcome-reported model, falling back to policy selection. Model filters retain all records for a matching request. Substitution permission requires an explicit ModelReplacementAllowed flag; rejection, model changes and backend admission do not establish permission. Cost comparisons require captured usage and prices for both models, report coverage, and are current-price same-usage counterfactual estimates rather than historical savings.

concepts.name: Recorded Capacity and Queue Pressure
concepts.definition: Pressure analysis identifies requests from recorded winning CapacityConstrained, CapacityCriticalWorkload, CapacityHighPriority, QueueDepthHigh and QueueCriticalPriority conditions. Its quota cohort recognizes MonthlyQuotaExceeded, DailyQuotaExceeded and DailyQuotaGovernance. These conditions do not provide measured utilization, queue depth, thresholds, balances or actual queue wait. RetryAfterMs is requested scheduling delay, not measured latency. Comparisons keep recorded-pressure and unknown-state cohorts separate, count requests independently from evaluations, and correlate latest in-window request outcomes without treating unflagged requests as proven unconstrained.

concepts.name: Recorded Latency and HTTP Outcome Analysis
concepts.definition: Latency and HTTP analysis selects the latest timestamp-ordered RequestOutcome per MID, not individual backend attempts or policy evaluations. Requests without captured HTTP outcomes remain separate, and rates use captured valid statuses. Error rate counts 4xx/5xx except 429; throttling rate counts HTTP 429 rather than policy Throttled decisions. Nearest-rank percentiles use finite nonnegative LatencyMs samples including measured zero, with coverage and invalid-value warnings. Unsampled timeline buckets remain gaps. Policy RetryAfterMs is requested scheduling delay; backend Retry-After headers, throttle/wake timestamps and normal-period baselines are not reconstructed.

concepts.name: Recorded Governance Evidence
concepts.definition: Governance reporting groups winning conditions into combined override/exception, daily-quota governance and entitled-workload budget signals. It does not separate administrator override from approved exception, incident response from audit/compliance, or premium from enterprise. Conditions and correlation IDs do not prove an approval operation or exemption. Charts and action tables count deduplicated evaluations; usage and recorded Cost are attributed once per governed MID from its latest in-window outcome, require UsageAvailable, and report coverage. Recorded Cost retains event units without assuming currency or verified billing; missing actors, reasons, approval references and policy versions remain unavailable.

concepts.name: Recorded Abuse and Content-Filter Signals
concepts.definition: Safety reporting requires AbuseDetected policy conditions or explicit positive jailbreak/content-filter flags on RequestOutcome records. It retains any positive signal across a MID's outcomes while displaying latest policy and HTTP outcomes separately. False or absent flags do not establish scanning or safety, and filtering followed by 2xx does not prove sanitization. Repeat activity requires captured identity on multiple distinct requests. Usage is attributed once from the latest outcome when UsageAvailable is true. Display and CSV use process-lifetime keyed HMAC request and tenant-scoped subject aliases, omit raw identifiers and prompt/response/error text, and retain workload names; these pseudonyms do not guarantee anonymity.

concepts.name: Investigator Vision Response Projection
concepts.definition: The CompanionApp projects observed vision JSON into caption, dense-caption, tag, object, person, OCR and image-metadata views while retaining the observed response as raw or formatted text. OCR collection recursively gathers text/content strings and removes exact duplicates. Display-text interpretation tries chat content before vision fields, then falls back to formatted JSON or the original response. Result tabs depend on captured section presence and metadata rather than assuming every analysis feature returned data.

concepts.name: CompanionApp Authentication
concepts.definition: CompanionApp has an independent authentication configuration under CompanionApp:Authentication. When enabled, it requires a selected provider: OAuth2 validates bearer tokens, GitHub uses OAuth with a session cookie, and Google uses OpenID Connect with a session cookie. Configured GitHub user, organization and team restrictions are alternatives; configured Google user and domain restrictions are alternatives. Razor component endpoints require the CompanionApp authorization policy, while static assets remain anonymous. Cookie sessions default to 60 minutes with sliding expiration; data-protection keys persist under .keys using the chat_tester application name. Disabling authentication leaves the CompanionApp unauthenticated.

concepts.name: CompanionApp Startup Configuration Bootstrap
concepts.definition: Outside --uionly mode, CompanionApp loads its configured App Configuration endpoint and initializes the configured label when it is absent or contains no settings. Label creation applies environment overrides and seeds proxy Event Hub logging only when the CompanionApp monitor is enabled and a destination is available; an existing populated label is not republished by this startup path. A configured profile-storage environment override supplies missing azblob URLs. Only profile URLs defaulted during this initialization trigger blob seeding: missing user-profile blobs receive configured sample users, missing suspension and application-ID blobs receive empty arrays, and existing user-profile blobs gain missing users through an ETag-conditional merge. This path does not create containers. Configuration and storage failures are logged without terminating startup.

concepts.name: CompanionApp Model Catalog Loading
concepts.definition: CompanionApp loads required chat and vision model configuration before registering application services. Chat configuration comes from chat-models.json unless CompanionApp:ChatModelsUrl selects an absolute file, HTTP or HTTPS URL. Local and file-URL chat configuration is registered for reload on change; HTTP(S) configuration is downloaded once during startup with a 30-second timeout. Optional environment-specific chat configuration is added afterward. Vision configuration uses required vision-models.json followed by an optional environment-specific file, both registered for reload on change. Unsupported chat URL schemes fail startup.

concepts.name: CompanionApp App Service Deployment
concepts.definition: CompanionApp provides an Azure App Service ZIP deployment path separate from its container-image publishing scripts. make-zip.sh restores and publishes CompanionApp.csproj, defaults to Release, disables the native app host, and archives the publish-directory contents as artifacts/companion-app-appservice.zip unless another output is supplied. upload_zip.sh deploys an existing ZIP to an existing named web app and resource group using Azure CLI. update_settings.sh separately exports JSON configuration through jq scalar paths into double-underscore-separated App Service application-setting keys. These scripts require their target resources to exist.

settings.name: AsyncBlobMaxQueue
settings.behavior_note: Async startup requires blob queue depth below this value; readiness accepts depth equal to this value. This does not set the blob pump queue capacity.

settings.name: PriorityWorkers
settings.behavior_note: PriorityWorkers is parsed at startup into the worker-priority dictionary; warm updates to PriorityWorker do not reassign existing workers.

settings.name: UserPriorityThreshold
settings.behavior_note: UserPriority snapshots this value at singleton construction; a warm refresh does not update the active threshold.

response_codes.name: Accepted
response_codes.cause: Async upgrade: client released early with blob URIs

response_codes.name: Bad Request
response_codes.cause: Malformed S7PTTL header value (InvalidTTL); unable to read the client request body; or invalid outbound header format.

response_codes.name: Forbidden
response_codes.cause: App ID not in allowlist (DisallowedAppID); inbound authentication failed (DisallowedKey); profile not found or user suspended (UnknownProfile); or Tokenomics policy rejected the request.

response_codes.name: Request Timeout
response_codes.cause: IO exception or task cancellation on backend communication

response_codes.name: Precondition Failed
response_codes.cause: Request TTL expired or the configured MultiPass backend-attempt limit was reached.

response_codes.name: Expectation Failed
response_codes.cause: Required header missing (IncompleteHeaders); header validation rule failed (InvalidHeader)

response_codes.name: Too Many Requests
response_codes.cause: Queue full; backend circuit check failed; no active hosts during SinglePass admission; max undrained events exceeded; or Tokenomics policy throttled the request.

response_codes.name: Internal Server Error
response_codes.cause: Unhandled exception; request body too large (ContentTooLarge)

response_codes.name: Bad Gateway
response_codes.cause: Backend attempts failed with different status codes or an unclassified transport error

response_codes.name: Service Unavailable
response_codes.cause: No host was attempted or backend name-resolution failures exhausted the available hosts.

request_headers.name: S7PPriorityKey
request_headers.definition: Priority tier value. Looked up in PriorityKeys to determine the request's priority level.

request_headers.name: S7PTTL
request_headers.definition: Per-request TTL: relative seconds as an integer or decimal, + followed by Unix seconds for an absolute timestamp, or a date/time string parsed as DateTimeOffset.

request_headers.name: S7PTimeout
request_headers.definition: Per-request per-host timeout override in milliseconds.

request_headers.name: S7P-Iterator
request_headers.definition: Per-request iteration mode override. Accepted values: SinglePass and MultiPass. Missing or invalid values use the current IterationMode default.

request_headers.name: S7PAsyncMode
request_headers.definition: Boolean true opts the request into async processing when the other eligibility requirements are satisfied.

request_headers.name: S7PDEBUG
request_headers.definition: Set to true to enable per-request debug tracing in logs.

request_headers.name: S7PREQUEUE
request_headers.definition: Set by a backend on a 429 response to signal the proxy should requeue the request.

request_headers.name: retry-after-ms
request_headers.definition: Preferred backend requeue delay in milliseconds.

request_headers.name: Retry-After
request_headers.definition: Backend requeue delay in integer seconds, used when retry-after-ms is absent or not a valid integer.

response_headers.name: Request-Queue-Duration
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds between recorded enqueue and dequeue timestamps, reported on forwarded backend responses.

response_headers.name: Request-Process-Duration
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds from the recorded dequeue timestamp to request-header enrichment before backend processing, reported on forwarded backend responses; this is not the final processing duration.

response_headers.name: BackendHost
response_headers.definition: Hostname of the backend that served the successful response.

response_headers.name: Total-Latency
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds from enqueue to the proxy's post-capture measurement, reported on forwarded backend responses.

response_headers.name: Attempts
response_headers.definition: Backend attempts made during the current dispatch cycle.

response_headers.name: Lifetime-Attempts
response_headers.definition: Cumulative backend attempts across all requeue cycles.

response_headers.name: x-Request-Queue-Duration
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds spent in the priority queue on exhausted-host error responses.

response_headers.name: x-Total-Latency
response_headers.definition: Total milliseconds from enqueue to an exhausted-host error response.

response_headers.name: x-ProxyHost
response_headers.definition: Proxy hostname included on exhausted-host error responses.

response_headers.name: x-MID
response_headers.definition: Message identifier included on exhausted-host error responses.

response_headers.name: x-Data-Blob-URI
response_headers.definition: Async response data blob URI returned with a 202 Accepted response.

response_headers.name: x-Header-Blob-URI
response_headers.definition: Async response header blob URI returned with a 202 Accepted response.

relationships.description: Remaining TTL bounds each synchronous attempt timeout; async-enabled attempts use AsyncTimeout and check expiration separately.
AsyncTriggerTimeout controls attempted client release; AsyncTimeout controls each async-enabled backend attempt, including before client release.
Path filter runs before load-balance ordering in the backend selection pipeline.
Load balancer orders hosts; circuit breaker gates each host before attempt.
Health poller results determine which hosts are in the active pool.
Health reporting uses the active list, while request circuit-breaker checks apply to candidates from the host snapshot.
OPEN circuits are skipped without consuming a MaxAttempts budget entry.
A Sentinel change triggers an attempted refresh of recognized nonempty Warm settings.
Non-probe requests that reach validation must pass before enqueue; probes bypass validation.
User profile supplies the allowlist header values consumed by header validation rules.
Async upgrade initiates background processing that ultimately produces a result blob.
Result blobs are deleted by the Azure Storage lifecycle policy, not by the proxy setting alone.
Supported response processors extract usage from backend responses.
CompositeEventClient fans out submitted serialized events to all registered backends.
Connection string format supports all modern options; legacy format is deprecated.
Direct-mode hosts are not probed and ordinarily report 0 ms average probe latency.
